laws.name: Texas Paid Sick Leave (Local Ordinances)
laws.statute_code: Note: No state-wide mandate; varies by local city ordinance
laws.description: Texas does not mandate paid sick leave statewide. However, some cities like Austin and Dallas have local ordinances requiring paid sick leave for certain employers.

other_requirements: Austin: Applies to employers with 15+ employees
Dallas: Applies to contractors and service workers

laws.notes: Texas has no state-wide paid sick leave requirement. Check local city ordinances for applicability. Some employers voluntarily provide sick leave.

laws.name: Texas Voting Leave
laws.description: Voters are entitled to reasonable time off to vote during early voting or on election day.

duration.notes: Reasonable time; typically up to 2 hours

other_requirements: Insufficient time outside work hours to vote

laws.notes: Employer cannot penalize employee for voting. Time is unpaid but may be required to be allowed.

laws.name: Texas Jury Duty Leave
laws.description: Employees cannot be punished for jury service. Employers are prohibited from discharging, threatening, or coercing employees for jury duty.
laws.notes: Protection applies to potential and actual jurors. Retaliation is a criminal offense in Texas.

laws.name: Federal FMLA as Applied in Texas
laws.statute_code: 29 U.S.C. § 2601 et seq. (Federal Law; applies to Texas employers with 50+ employees)
laws.description: Texas employers with 50+ employees must comply with federal FMLA. Texas does not provide broader state-level protections.

other_requirements: Worked at least 1,250 hours in past 12 months

laws.notes: Texas employers with 50+ employees must comply with FMLA. Smaller employers are generally not required to provide protected leave unless covered by local ordinances.

laws.name: Texas Military Leave
laws.description: Employees who are members of the Texas Military Department are entitled to military leave during inactive duty training and active duty.

duration.notes: Per fiscal year for inactive duty training; unlimited for active duty

other_requirements: Called to active duty or training

laws.notes: Applies to employers with Texas military members. Also includes federal military duty protections under USERRA.
